author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected after the fact. The correction is held to the same rules as booking and updates the existing visit in place, never leaving the pet with an extra visit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form is shown carrying the visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit's date and description are updated in place and the pet gains no further visit.
Given a valid correction, when it is submitted, then the owner's record is shown.
Given a correction with a blank description, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a correction with a date of today or earlier, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a booked visit, when it is corrected, then the pet's other visits are left untouched.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit remains out of scope (NG-5).
notes: Product owner fixed the surface for the design stage: GET and POST at /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; the GET reuses template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with a visit model attribute prefilled from the current record; the POST validates as booking does and redirects to the owner detail page on success, redisplays the form on failure. New behavior must be covered by tests.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correcting a booked visit extends the create-or-update-by-identity pattern already used for owners and pets (docs/system-design.md § State Machine; § Contracts) to visits. Booking and correction share VisitController, the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template, and the single write path — owner.save(owner) cascading through OwnerRepository (§ Overview, § Contracts). The one genuinely new element is an in-place-update access path: a Visit resolved by identity within the owner->pet->visit aggregate and mutated in place. No such path exists today — VisitController only ever constructs and adds a new Visit. This is a small adjustment to an existing pattern, not new ground; no ADR (the product decision is already in adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, and in-place update is the same insert-vs-update branch PetController already teaches).
integration_points: New route pair GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController
Edit path must resolve the EXISTING Visit by visitId (navigation by identity within the pet) and bind onto it, then owners.save(owner) cascades the mutated Visit; no addVisit call on the edit path

doc-sync follow-up: after this lands, update the VisitController row in docs/system-design.md § Contracts to add REQ-VIS-003 and 'correcting a booked visit in place' (do not pre-write it now — the doc records current state)

patterns.description: getPet(Integer) — navigation-by-identity within the aggregate; mirror it with a Pet.getVisit(Integer) helper (or resolve inline over pet.getVisits()) to locate the visit to correct
processNewVisitForm — the validation + aggregate-save + redirect-to-owner shape the edit POST mirrors; date-future check at line 100, redirect at line 111
§ State Machine records the isNew insert-vs-update branch already used by pet workflows — the precedent for choosing update over insert

risks.risk: TRAP: the shared @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:63) unconditionally does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit). It fires before EVERY mapping in the controller. If it runs unchanged on the edit route it grafts a spurious visit onto the pet, directly violating the acceptance criterion 'the pet gains no further visit'. Durable memory does not warn about this.
risks.mitigation: Make the loader visitId-aware: when a visitId path variable is present, resolve and return the existing Visit (throwing if it does not belong to the pet, mirroring the pet-not-found guard at lines 71-74) and do NOT call addVisit; when absent, keep the new-Visit behavior. Or split into a distinct loader for the edit route. The edit path must never call pet.addVisit / owner.addVisit.

risks.risk: Visit identity could be tampered via a form-supplied id (mass assignment).
risks.mitigation: Derive the target visit solely from the path variable resolved through the owner->pet->visit ownership chain; keep setAllowedFields disallowing 'id','*.id' (VisitController.java:52-54). This matches the mass-assignment mitigation in docs/system-design.md § Threat Model.

risks.risk: The form (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:30) has no th:action, so it posts back to the URL that rendered it — correct by default for both /new and /edit. Adding a th:action would break one of the two.
risks.mitigation: Leave the form actionless; the edit GET renders at the /edit URL and the browser posts back to it. No template action change needed — this is why the PRD reuses the template as-is.

risks.risk: The template branches on visit['new']: an existing (non-new) visit hides the 'New' heading, renders the 'Previous Visits' table (including the visit being edited), and the submit button still reads #{addVisit} 'Add Visit'. Cosmetic only; not in the acceptance criteria.
risks.mitigation: Leave the template per the PRD-fixed surface. Flag the button-label mismatch as known cosmetic debt; changing copy would touch all eleven message bundles (REQ-LANG-002) and is out of this slice's scope.

risks.risk: The future-date rule is a controller check (VisitController.java:100), not a bean-validation constraint, so @Valid alone will not enforce it on the edit POST.
risks.mitigation: Repeat the same result.rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate') check on the edit POST; extracting a shared private helper is the clean TDD Refactor-step option once both POSTs are green. Description-required stays covered by @NotBlank on Visit via @Valid.

notes: Verdict minor, not covered: durable memory covers booking, aggregate save, and the insert-vs-update precedent, but there is no recorded in-place-update path for a visit and the shared @ModelAttribute loader is an active trap on the edit route — that guidance is the design value here. Oracle not connected this run; architectural_fit confirmed via Read of Owner.java, Pet.java (no getVisit(Integer) exists — confirmed), Visit.java, VisitController.java, and createOrUpdateVisitForm.html — grep/read basis, IDE not consulted. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods use the `should{Outcome}` form instead of the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` BDD school mandated by testing-principles.md § Test Naming (effective 2026-07-31). New tests must follow the school. Example renames: `shouldShowEditVisitFormPrefilledWithCurrentDetails` → `theEditVisitFormShouldBePrefilledWithCurrentDetails`; `shouldUpdateVisitInPlaceAndRedirectToOwnerOnValidEdit` → `theValidEditShouldRedirectToOwner`; `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting` → `theEditShouldNotAddAFurtherVisitToPet`; `shouldRejectEditWithBlankDescriptionAndRedisplayForm` → `theEditWithBlankDescriptionShouldRedisplayTheForm`; `shouldRejectEditWithPastDateAndRedisplayForm` → `theEditWithPastDateShouldRedisplayTheForm`.
findings.fix: Rename all five new test methods to follow `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`.

findings.description: `shouldUpdateVisitInPlaceAndRedirectToOwnerOnValidEdit` names an in-place update as its behavior but only asserts the redirect status and view name. The in-place mutation is verified in a separate test. The name overpromises: a reader expects this test to verify the visit fields were updated and the ID preserved. Either rename this test to express only the redirect concern, or absorb the in-place-update assertions from `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting` here and give that test a narrower name.
findings.fix: Rename to `theValidEditShouldRedirectToOwner` (narrow scope) OR move in-place assertions into this test and rename `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting` to cover the no-extra-visit concern only.

findings.description: The string `"Corrected description"` is a bare Tier 3 (mystery) literal repeated in three test methods, and `LocalDate.now().plusDays(3)` is inlined without a name in `shouldUpdateVisitInPlaceAndRedirectToOwnerOnValidEdit`. By the three-tier naming convention (testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention), these should be named class-level constants (e.g., `CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION`, `CORRECTED_DATE`) so readers can distinguish scaffolding from meaningful values at a glance.
findings.fix: Declare `private static final String CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION = "Corrected description";` and `private static final LocalDate CORRECTED_DATE = LocalDate.now().plusDays(3);` at class level and replace the bare literals.

findings.description: `TEST_VISIT_ID` is a new constant added by this slice. The value is meaningful: it is the identity the tests assert on in `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting`. The three-tier convention (Tier 1: role-describing name) calls for `EXISTING_VISIT_ID`, not `TEST_VISIT_ID` — the `TEST_` prefix pattern is from the pre-existing constants and predates the naming school.
findings.fix: Rename to `EXISTING_VISIT_ID` and update all references.

findings.description: The `init()` method was modified in this slice to seed an existing `Visit`. testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction states "a slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory." `init()` constructs `Owner`, `Pet`, and `Visit` via direct constructor calls. A factory method (e.g., `createOwnerWithPetAndExistingVisit()`) would isolate callers from constructor-signature changes and make the setup intent readable at a glance.
findings.fix: Extract the init body into a private factory method and call it from `@BeforeEach init()`.

findings.description: In `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting`, the Arrange phase (line 149: `LocalDate correctedDate = ...`) is not separated from the Act phase (`mockMvc.perform(...)`) by a blank line. testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure requires phases to be separated by blank lines.
findings.fix: Add a blank line after `LocalDate correctedDate = LocalDate.now().plusDays(3);`.

findings.description: Acceptance criterion 6 — 'the pet's other visits are left untouched' — is only partially covered. The fixture seeds a single visit; `shouldNotAddAdditionalVisitWhenEditingExisting` verifies the post-edit visit count is 1 (no extra added), but does not exercise the case where a second, unrelated visit is present and must survive the edit. A second visit in the fixture would close this gap with a `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` or size assertion.
findings.fix: Seed a second visit (distinct ID and description) in `init()` and assert post-edit that the pet has exactly 2 visits, with the second unchanged.
